_comment: Gate calibration controls (S0). The gate has never been run against real
weights, so its threshold is set from what the POSITIVE controls actually
measure rather than chosen a priori, and a NEGATIVE control that passes
means the gate cannot detect a known-bad configuration.
The two negatives are not hypothetical: `arm4_f2_construction` is the rope
dict that replaced Llama-3.1-8B's shipped `llama3` block in the ARM4 f2
cell, where the target emitted EOS at token 0 and the acceptance collapse
was published as a result. `llama2_misanchored` is YaRN anchored on the
context length instead of the 4096 base, which measured 57x native
expect: "pass" | "fail" is the REQUIRED verdict. A control that
disagrees means the gate is wrong, not the control.

P3_native_128k carries native_baseline=true: it is the reference every other candidate is judged against, so it must be selected by declaration rather than by falling back to whichever row happens to be first with context <= 128k (which picked the 32k control and mislabelled it native_ppl_at_128k).

candidates.name: N1_arm4_f2_construction
candidates._what_it_reproduces: The rope dict that replaced Llama-3.1-8B's shipped llama3 block in the ARM4 f2 cell, where the target emitted EOS at token 0.

candidates.name: N2_llama2_misanchored
candidates._what_it_reproduces: The historical bug: no anchor override, so transformers 4.47.1 routes the YaRN band onto config.max_position_embeddings = the context length. This is the construction that measured 826.9 perplexity at 32k vs 14.45 correctly anchored.
